newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha flat, ADNOC cuts term offer to $21.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha flat, ADNOC cuts term offer to $21.

text.p: Naphtha prices were barely changed in thin activity on Monday as most traders kept to the sidelines, watching progress in naphtha term talks between Asian clients and Middle Eastern suppliers, traders said.

In the latest development in term negotiations between Abu Dhabi National Oil Co (ADNOC) and east Asian buyers, the supplier was said to have lowered its offer price to $21.00 per tonne over the ADNOC formula from its previous offer of $21.75.
ADNOC initially started talks for one-year supply contracts starting in July with an offer price of $22.50.
In term talks between about a dozen Asian term lifters and Kuwait Petroleum Corp (KPC), both sides are gradually narrowing differences, traders said.
KPC originally offered a price of $20 per tonne over the mean of Middle Eastern quotes for annual term contracts that begin in August while initial bids ranged from about $8.00 to $13.50, they said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half August stood at $203.50/205.00 per tonne, while first-half September was valued at around $204.00/205.50 in quiet trade, traders said.
